text:
Seattle went to Helsinki for the Global Series, gave Jagger Firkus his NHL debut, saw Kaapo Kakko play at home in Finland, and lost both games to Carolina, the second 5-1 with 19% of the chances. Lane Lambert said "we weren't nearly good enough," per Alison Lukan. The Kraken have scored 1, 1 and 3 in a three-game losing streak, and Daily Faceoff's line that Cutter Gauthier has twice as many goals as the whole team since Oct. 29 is the kind of stat that follows you home. Lambert called the coming run against Pacific teams important. This is the first of it.

Vancouver arrives with its own trouble and a little momentum. The Canucks have the league's worst five-on-five process, 40% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances), and they allow the most expected goals per 60. Yet they won in Vegas and Utah on the weekend, the second with 34% of the chances and Nikita Tolopilo saving 4.0 goals more than expected, after which he was sent back to the AHL. Leevi Meriläinen is in net tonight. Brock Boeser has an eight-game point streak. The noise is about who leaves: David Pagnotta told Daily Faceoff Vancouver is "open for business," with Filip Hronek's name in it, and Jake DeBrusk trade talk is "gaining momentum," per Markerzone. Vancouver's playoff chance in our simulations rounds to zero.

The Kraken are healthier on paper, 44% of the chances at five on five, but Jared McCann is out until about Jan. 2, and Shane Wright has moved onto the top power play and up to 17:18 a night. Philipp Grubauer is at .863 over his last five starts. Jordan Eberle has eight points in four games against Vancouver, and Berkly Catton has 10 points in 10, more on bounces than chances by our reading. Jamie Oleksiak makes his first trip back after 389 games as a Kraken.

Our model leans Seattle, 3.20 to 2.74 in expected goals. Our sleepers: Vince Dunn at 51% for a point against the league's leakiest defense, and Drew O'Connor, 15% to score.
headline: Kraken come home from Finland needing a win
